Package common.core.controllers

Class PIDFFConfig

java.lang.Object
common.core.controllers.PIDFFConfig
public class PIDFFConfig extends Object
The gains (tuning numbers) for a mechanism's control loop: PID plus feedforward.

What the gains do

Every gain turns something into volts for the motor. Units are whatever the mechanism measures in, e.g. meters for an elevator or degrees for an arm.

Feedback (PID) pushes based on how far off the mechanism is, the error:

  • kP: volts per unit of error. The main gain: bigger pushes harder, too big overshoots and wobbles.
  • kI: volts per unit of error, per second it's been off. Slowly builds up to fix a small error that won't go away. Usually 0.
  • kD: volts per unit/second the error is changing. Brakes as the mechanism closes in, to reduce overshoot. Often 0.

Feedforward pushes based on what the mechanism needs, before there's any error:

  • kS: volts to overcome friction and get it moving at all.
  • kV: volts per unit/second of speed, to keep it moving at that speed. The main gain for a flywheel.
  • kA: volts per unit/second^2 of acceleration. Not used by the motor controllers.
  • kG: volts to hold it up against gravity: constant for an elevator, times the cosine of the angle for an arm, so it's strongest when the arm is level.

Good feedforward does most of the work and leaves PID only small errors to fix, which makes a mechanism fast and smooth. Tune feedforward first, e.g. with SysId, then add kP.

Feedforward gains are stored as DoubleSuppliers rather than numbers so they can come from a Shuffleboard box while tuning: type in a new number, and the next read gets the new value.

      Sets what kG is multiplied by in positionFF(double, boolean) and velocityFF(double, double, boolean), e.g. the cosine of an arm's angle when the roboRIO runs the loop. Mechanisms whose loop runs on the motor controller handle arm gravity there instead, so don't need this.

    • positionFF

      public double positionFF(double pidOutput, boolean atSetpoint)
      Feedforward volts for a mechanism moving to a position, when the roboRIO runs its loop: kS in the direction it's being pushed, plus kG. There's no kV, since the setpoint is a position, not a speed.
      Parameters:
      pidOutput - This loop's PID output, used to pick kS's direction.
      atSetpoint - Whether it's already there; kS is left out then, so it doesn't jitter.

    • velocityFF

      public double velocityFF(double setpoint, double pidOutput, boolean atSetpoint)
      Feedforward volts for a mechanism spinning at a speed, when the roboRIO runs its loop: kS in the direction it's being pushed, kV times the speed, plus kG.
      Parameters:
      setpoint - The target speed.
      pidOutput - This loop's PID output, used to pick kS's direction.
      atSetpoint - Whether it's already at speed; kS is left out then, so it doesn't jitter.
